learningObjectives.title: The Analysing and Evaluating Performance (AEP) task

questions.q: What percentage of the total OCR GCSE PE & Sport Science (J587) qualification does the non-exam assessment (NEA) account for?
questions.explain: The NEA (Performance in Physical Education) is worth 40% of the total J587 qualification.

questions.q: In how many practical activities must a student be assessed for the NEA?
questions.explain: Students are assessed in three different practical activities for the NEA.

questions.q: For the three assessed activities, students must include at least:
options: One individual and one team activity
questions.explain: At least one individual and one team activity must be included among the three assessed activities.

questions.q: How many marks is each assessed practical activity worth?
questions.explain: Each of the three practical activities is marked out of 20, giving 60 marks in total.

questions.q: Each 20-mark practical activity is divided into which two components?
options: 10 marks for skills in isolation and 10 marks for a competitive situation
15 marks for fitness and 5 marks for skill
20 marks for a full game only
10 marks for theory and 10 marks for practical
questions.explain: Each activity awards 10 marks for skills in isolation and 10 marks for performance in a full competitive situation.

questions.q: Activities selected for assessment must be chosen from:
questions.explain: Only activities on the OCR approved activities list can be used for assessment.

questions.q: 'Skills in isolation' in the practical assessment refers to:
options: Performing skills in a full competitive game
Demonstrating skills and techniques in a practice or drill situation
questions.explain: Skills in isolation are demonstrated in practices or drills, separate from a full competitive game.

questions.q: Why are practical performances usually recorded on video?
options: To allow the student to self-assess only
To provide evidence for external moderation by OCR
Because live assessment is not permitted
questions.explain: Video evidence allows OCR to externally moderate the marks awarded by the centre.

questions.q: Practical performances are initially marked by:
questions.explain: The NEA is internally assessed, so the centre's teachers mark the practical performances first.

questions.q: The process by which OCR checks that centres have marked practical work to the correct standard is called:
questions.explain: OCR uses external moderation to confirm that centres have applied the mark scheme accurately.

questions.q: How many marks is the Analysing and Evaluating Performance (AEP) task worth?
questions.explain: The AEP task is marked out of 20.

questions.q: The AEP task accounts for what percentage of the total GCSE qualification?
questions.explain: The 20-mark AEP task is worth 10% of the overall GCSE.

questions.q: In the 'analyse' element of the AEP, a student is required to:
options: Only describe the rules of the activity
Identify strengths and weaknesses in a performance
questions.explain: Analysing involves identifying the strengths and weaknesses of a performance.

questions.q: The 'evaluate' element of the AEP requires students to:
options: Explain the causes of weaknesses and suggest how performance could improve
questions.explain: Evaluating goes beyond identifying weaknesses to explaining their causes and how to improve them.

questions.q: The AEP typically concludes with:
options: An action plan setting out how to improve the identified weaknesses
questions.explain: The AEP culminates in an action plan proposing how to improve the weaknesses identified.

questions.q: A student identifies that a footballer's main weakness is muscular endurance in the legs. Which method is MOST appropriate for their action plan?
options: Circuit or interval training targeting leg muscular endurance
questions.explain: Muscular endurance is best developed through circuit or interval training using moderate loads and high repetitions.

questions.q: A netball player's action plan aims to improve agility. Which method is most suitable to include?
questions.explain: Agility is trained through ladder and shuttle drills that combine speed with rapid changes of direction.

questions.q: In an action plan, applying the principles of training (e.g. progressive overload) ensures that:
options: Training is gradually and appropriately overloaded to bring improvement
questions.explain: Progressive overload gradually increases training demands so the body adapts and performance improves.

questions.q: Applying theoretical knowledge to improve performance in the AEP might include recommending appropriate:
options: Training methods, principles of training and types of skill practice
Only the rules of the game
questions.explain: Improvement suggestions should draw on theory such as training methods, training principles and practice types.

questions.q: A gymnast identifies poor flexibility as a weakness. The most appropriate improvement method is:
questions.explain: Flexibility is improved through stretching methods such as static and PNF stretching.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) PE & Sport Science (J587) specification; Performance in Physical Education (NEA)
